title: Cell-surface biotinylation of GABAA receptors in mouse hippocampal slices after sevoflurane anesthesia
protocol: Turn on the heating pad underneath the induction chamber.
Adjust the airflow to deliver a mixture of 2.3% sevoflurane, 30% O2, and 70% medical air at approximately 1 L/min.
Monitor expired gases with a gas analyzer to ensure appropriate O2 concentration.
Replace the air in the induction chamber with the delivered gas mixture.
Once saturated, open the induction chamber quickly and place the mouse inside.
Wait for the mouse to lose consciousness.
Gently tilt the induction chamber to assess loss of righting reflex (LORR).
Confirm LORR when the mouse is supine with all four paws not touching the floor.
Reassess LORR every 30 seconds if the mouse rights itself.
Continuously deliver sevoflurane, medical air, and oxygen for 2 hours.
Monitor the mouse visually for cyanosis and hypoventilation during anesthesia.
Ensure the breathing rate is approximately 55–65 breaths per minute.
Maintain the mouse in a supine position throughout the anesthetic treatment.
Increase air flow rate to 3 L/min after 2 hours to flush sevoflurane.
Allow the mouse to recover in the warmed chamber for at least 10 min or until it regains consciousness before returning it to the home cage.
Sacrifice mice using decapitation.
Quickly extract the brain and keep it in ice-cold carbonated aCSF.
Make two coronal cuts in the mouse brain as denoted by the dotted lines using a razor blade.
Use super glue to adhere the rostral end of the brain onto the metal vibratome plate.
Attach the metal plate to the vibratome such that the brain is submerged in the vibratome reservoir containing ice-cold aCSF, and surrounded by ice.
Ensure constant bubbling with carbogen during slicing.
Cut coronal slices with a thickness of 300–350 μm.
Carefully remove hippocampal slices from the coronal slices using regular dissecting scalpels.
Transfer four hippocampal slices into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube using a Pasteur pipette.
Allow the slices to recover on ice with 1 ml of cold aCSF for 5–10 minutes before starting the biotinylation procedure.
After the recovery, keep the four hippocampal slices in the same Eppendorf tube.
Wash the slices with 500 μL of ice-cold aCSF.
Repeat the washing twice.
Use P1000 tips to remove aCSF from the top of the tube during washes.
Use P200 tips to carefully remove remaining aCSF near the slices at the bottom without disturbing them.
Add 1 mL of biotinylation solution (aCSF containing 0.5 mg/mL of Sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin) to each tube.
Incubate on ice for 1 hour, swirling gently every 15 minutes.
Remove the biotinylation solution carefully and wash the slices with 500 μL of ice-cold aCSF twice.
Add 1 mL of quenching buffer to each tube to remove any unbound Sulfo-NHS-SS-biotin.
Incubate for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the quenching buffer carefully from each tube.
Wash the slices with 1 mL of ice-cold aCSF twice.
Remove aCSF from the tubes.
Add 500 μL of ice-cold lysis buffer to each tube.
Sonicate the samples twice, each time for 5 s with a 5-s rest in between using a probe sonicator (setting: 5 ms pulse, 70% amplitude) while keeping the tubes on ice.
Rotate the tubes containing the lysate at 4°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the tubes containing the lysate for 30 min at 12,500 RPM and 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes and discard the pellet.
Keep the tubes on ice.
Transfer 50 μL of supernatant to new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Add 50 μL of 2× Laemmli buffer to each tube.
Store the tubes in a freezer at −30°C until further analysis.
Add 100 μL of NeutraAvidin beads (no prior washing required) to the Eppendorf tubes containing the remaining supernatant.
Rotate tubes at 4°C for 2 h or overnight, ensuring an equal volume of beads is added to each tube.
Wash NeutraAvidin beads with lysis buffer to remove unbound proteins.
Centrifuge the tubes containing the NeutraAvidin beads for 3 minutes at 2,500 RPM and 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Add 500 μL of lysis buffer.
Rotate for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the lysis buffer carefully to avoid disturbing the beads at the bottom of the tube.
Repeat washing steps three times.
Add 50 μL of 2× Laemmli sample buffer to each tube.
Store the tubes in a freezer at −30°C until use.
Heat both the biotinylation and total protein fraction on a heating block at 70°C for 7 minutes.
Spin down the samples briefly to ensure the beads are settled at the bottom of the tube.
Carefully collect the sample without touching the beads inside the tube.
Load 10 μL of each protein fraction in the same gel for comparison by Western blotting.
Separate proteins via SDS-PAGE and transfer them to polyvinylidene difluoride membranes.
Block membranes with 5% skim milk in T-TBS.
Incubate primary antibodies for α5 subunit of GABAA receptors, Na/K-ATPase, and β-actin at dilutions of 1:1000 overnight.
Incubate secondary antibodies (anti-rabbit or anti-mouse) at dilutions of 1:5000 for one hour.
